suggestions.title: 1. Your GUT-SIGNS answers as they went in, and two things I left out
suggestions.whose: his own: his round-59 answers 2.1 and 2.2, made into paragraphs for the reader by me; "A gut-driven mental hell is often mistaken as shadow work." is his line, word for word
suggestions.question:
The four highlighted paragraphs hold your answers. From 2.1: loss of bodily control is "someone wetting or soiling themselves, or not being able to sit up, stand, walk or talk", and neurological disorganization is "my catch-all for that loss of control plus a whole lot more". From 2.2: "address the gut first" and "You don't need to try to tell which is from what", and under Gut-Toxin & Die-Off Tools the paragraph that starts "After all, nausea and diarrhea are common on psychedelics".
Two things I left out, and one I added:
1.1 The list of symptoms GPT gave for neurological disorganization. Most of it (confusion, shaking, light and sound being too much) is what any strong trip brings, so a friend could not use it to tell. I linked your brain checks instead, which are tests a friend can do.
1.2 "if the gut is fine obviously it's not related to the gut". Two fresh readers said it told them nothing, and a fine gut does not rule out the brain, which the paragraph before it names.
1.3 Added: losing control of the body "is on the list to call medics for". Wetting or soiling themselves, not being able to walk normally and losing the ability to speak are all on your Call Medics For list, and without the pointer a reader could treat someone who cannot talk or walk with a remedy only.
(a) fine as they are; (b) put back what I left out, or take out what I added (say which); or edit any of the four.
suggestions.why: the words come from your answers, I chose what to leave out of them, and the call-medics pointer is mine from your own list
suggestions.stays: the four paragraphs, which are in the guide now
suggestions.advice_note: (a); fairly sure. If you want examples for neurological disorganization, name the ones a trip does not bring by itself

suggestions.title: 2. ZeoCharge & Ferment: six things about zeolite only you know
suggestions.whose: the post's paragraphs, drafted by a model from his practice
suggestions.question:
These four paragraphs still read below High. The two on taking zeolite read Human, but Low and Medium, as they stand ([check](https://www.pangram.com/history/25652097-7c2d-444d-ab06-9e9af3c993c1)) and after two small joins ([check](https://www.pangram.com/history/86a0478d-42dc-4596-8cc8-ff8b777f8734)). The two on ozonating read AI as they stand ([check](https://www.pangram.com/history/859d5bdf-7aeb-4f53-b5d5-9f7bf44ca04f)) and after a first small try ([check](https://www.pangram.com/history/07cec6fa-57a0-406c-b839-0bd71249e4ec)). I can't find more AI tells in them that I know how to fix, and apart from the facts you gave, none of it is your own writing. What three fresh readers could not get from them is facts:
2.1 Is the fermented beet juice the ZHoly3O ferment, or a different one?
2.2 How much water for the spoonful of zeolite, and do you repeat it if the nausea keeps on?
2.3 Rubbing it on the body: the dry powder, or the mix in water?
2.4 "Many products did nothing for me, and quality mattered enormously." How does a reader tell a good zeolite before a trip, when sober people don't feel much? Is the answer ZeoCharge?
2.5 "Most zeolites have clogged pores because they haven't been cleaned." Is the ozonating what cleans them?
2.6 How much powder and water go under the ozone for those ten minutes?
A line on any of them and I'll write it in; or say which to leave unanswered.
suggestions.why: a reader deciding what to buy or make cannot act on these paragraphs yet, and each answer gives a sentence something to say
suggestions.stays: the four paragraphs as they are in your post
suggestions.advice_note: 2.1, 2.4 and 2.5 first: they change what a reader buys or makes
